description.p: TECHNICAL FIELD

[0001] The present disclosure relates to a batterypack having a path through which a coolant introduced therein may flow when a thermal runaway phenomenon occurs, a battery rack and an energy storage system (ESS) including the battery pack, and more specifically, to a battery pack having a structure in which a coolant introduced therein may smoothly move between unit modules adjacent to each other when water is injected into a battery pack at which a thermal runaway phenomenon occurs, and a battery rack and an ESS including the battery module.
[0002] The present application claims priority to Korean Patent Application No. 10-2019-0063999 filed on May 30, 2019 in the Republic of Korea.
[0003] The present application claims priority to Korean Patent Application No. 10-2019-0068053 filed on June 10, 2019 in the Republic of Korea.
BACKGROUND ART

[0004] In a battery pack that includes a plurality of battery cells, if an abnormality such as a short circuit occurs in some battery cells to raise temperature continuously so that the temperature of the battery cell exceeds a critical temperature, a thermal runaway phenomenon occurs. If a thermal runaway phenomenon occurs in some battery cells as described above, safety issues may be generated.

[0005] If a flame or the like is generated due to the thermal runaway phenomenon occurring in some battery cells, the flame rapidly raises the temperature of adjacent battery cells, and thus the thermal runaway phenomenon may be propagated to adjacent cells within a short time.

[0006] Eventually, if the thermal runaway phenomenon occurring in some battery cells is not quickly responded, it may lead to disasters such as ignition and explosion of a battery module or a battery pack, which is a battery unit with a greater capacity than the battery cell, and this may not only result in property damage but also cause safety problems.

[0007] Thus, if a flame occurs due to the thermal runaway phenomenon in some battery cells inside the battery pack, it is urgently necessary to quickly lower the temperature inside the battery pack to prevent the flame from spreading further.

[0008] A cell stack accommodated inside the battery module has a structure in which a pad for securing a space capable of absorbing swelling is interposed between every adjacent unit modules, using a certain number of battery cells as one unit module.

[0009] In the battery pack having the above structure, if a thermal runaway phenomenon occurs therein, even though a coolant is introduced into the battery pack, the coolant may not flow smoothly between adjacent unit modules due to the pad.
[0010] Therefore, it is demanded to develop a battery pack having a structure capable of ensuring a smooth flow of coolant while employing the pad-inserted structure.

[0011] In addition, a battery pack adopting an air-cooled structure has an air channel through which a coolant leaks without staying inside even though the coolant is introduced to lower the temperature inside the battery pack and extinguish the flame. Thus, it is demanded to develop a battery rack having a structure capable of blocking the air channel when a coolant is introduced into a battery pack where a thermal runaway phenomenon has occurred.
[0012] Further prior art is described in US 2013/252063 A1 , US 2015/200429 A1 , JP 2000 048867 A and US 2017/200993 A1 .
DISCLOSURE
Technical Problem

[0013] The present disclosure is designed to solve the problems of the related art, and therefore the present disclosure is directed to preventing a flame from spreading greatly by rapidly lowering the temperature inside a battery pack when the flame is generated in some battery cells in the battery pack due to a thermal runaway phenomenon.

[0014] However, the technical problem to be solved by the present disclosure is not limited to the above, and other objects not mentioned herein will be understood from the following description by those skilled in the art.
Technical Solution

[0015] In one aspect of the present disclosure, there is provided a battery pack, comprising: a unit module stack formed by stacking a plurality of unit modules, each unit module having a plurality of battery cells stacked on each other; a swelling absorption pad interposed between the unit modules adjacent to each other; and a pack housing configured to accommodate the unit module stack and the swelling absorption pad, wherein the swelling absorption pad has a coolant channel formed to extend along a longitudinal direction thereof.

[0016] The coolant channel may include an input port provided to one side of the swelling absorption pad in the longitudinal direction; an output port provided to the other side of the swelling absorption pad in the longitudinal direction; and a cooling portion configured to connect the input port and the output port to each other and having a greater sectional area than the input port and the output port.
[0017] The coolant channel may be open such that a coolant flowing through the coolant channel directly contacts a pair of battery cells in contact with the swelling absorption pad.
[0018] The input port may be located higher than the output port.

[0019] The battery pack may include an air inlet formed through the pack housing at one side of the unit module stack in a stacking direction; and an air outlet formed through the pack housing at the other side of the unit module stack in the stacking direction. The battery pack may further include an expansion pad disposed inside the air inlet and the air outlet and configured to expand due to the contact with a coolant introduced into the battery pack to close the air inlet and the air outlet.
[0020] The battery pack may include a pair of bus bar frames respectively coupled to one side and the other side of the unit module stack in a width direction.
[0021] The air inlet and the air outlet may be formed at locations corresponding an empty space formed between the bus bar frame and the pack housing.

[0022] The battery pack may include a coolant tube insert hole formed through the pack housing from one side or the other side of the unit module stack in the stacking direction to communicate with an empty space formed between the bus bar frame and the pack housing.
[0023] A battery rack according to an embodiment of the present disclosure includes a plurality of battery packs according to an embodiment of the present disclosure as described above.

[0024] An energy storage system (ESS) according to an embodiment of the present disclosure includes a plurality of battery packs according to an embodiment of the present disclosure as described above.
Advantageous Effects

[0025] According to one aspect of the present disclosure, when a flame is generated in some battery cells inside the battery pack due to a thermal runaway phenomenon, it is possible to prevent the flame from spreading further by lowering the temperature inside the battery pack quickly. That is, it is possible to quickly lower the temperature inside the battery pack by solving the problem that a coolant is not able to flow smoothly between adjacent unit modules due to a pad when the coolant is introduced into the battery pack having a structure in which the pad for absorbing swelling is interposed between adjacent unit modules.

[0026] In addition, according to another aspect of the present disclosure, in a battery rack including an air-cooled battery pack, when a water coolant is introduced into the battery pack where a thermal runaway phenomenon occurs, it is possible to effectively prevent the thermal runaway phenomenon from propagating by adopting a structure in which the air channel for cooling is blocked so that the coolant stays inside the battery pack.

BEST MODE

[0028] Hereinafter, preferred embodiments of the present disclosure will be described in detail with reference to the accompanying drawings. Prior to the description, it should be understood that the terms used in the specification and the appended claims should not be construed as limited to general and dictionary meanings, but interpreted based on the meanings and concepts corresponding to technical aspects of the present disclosure on the basis of the principle that the inventor is allowed to define terms appropriately for the best explanation. Therefore, the description proposed herein is just a preferable example for the purpose of illustrations only.

[0029] Referring to FIG. 1 , an energy storage system (ESS) according to an embodiment of the present disclosure includes a plurality of battery racks 100 according to an embodiment of the present disclosure.

[0030] Referring to FIGS. 1 to 3 , the battery rack 100 according to an embodiment of the present disclosure includes a rack housing 110, at least one battery pack 120, a water tank 130, a controller 140, a coolant tube 150 and a sensor 160.

[0031] The rack housing 110 is an approximately rectangular frame that defines the appearance of the battery rack 100, and has a space formed therein so that the plurality of battery packs 120, the water tank 130, the controller 140, the coolant tube 150 and the sensor 160 may be installed therein.

[0032] The battery pack 120 is provided in plural, and the plurality of battery packs 120 are vertically stacked in the rack housing 110 to form a single pack stack. The specific structure of the battery pack 120 will be described later in detail with reference to FIGS. 4 to 10 .

[0033] The water tank 130 is provided inside the rack housing 110 and stores a water coolant that is to be supplied to the battery pack 120 when a thermal runaway phenomenon occurs at the battery pack 120. The water tank 130 may be disposed above the pack stack for quick and smooth supply of coolant. In this case, even though a separate coolant pump is not used, the coolant may be rapidly supplied into the battery pack 120 by free fall and water pressure of the coolant. Of course, a separate coolant pump may also be applied to the water tank 130 to supply the coolant more quickly and smoothly.

[0034] The controller 140 may be connected to the sensor 160 and the water tank 130 and output a control signal to open the water tank 130 according to the sensing signal of the sensor 160. In addition, the controller 140 may additionally perform a function as a battery management system (BMS) that is connected to each battery pack 120 to manage charging and discharging thereof, in addition to the above function.

[0035] The controller 140 outputs a control signal to open the water tank 130 when detecting gas or a temperature rise above a reference value inside the battery rack 100 due to a thermal runaway phenomenon occurring in at least one of the plurality of battery packs 120, and allows the coolant to be supplied into the battery pack 120 accordingly.

[0036] If the water tank 130 is opened according to the control signal of the controller 140, the coolant is sequentially supplied from a battery pack 120 located at a relatively upper portion to a battery pack 120 located at a relatively lower portion. Thus, the flame in the battery packs 120 is extinguished and also the battery packs 120 are cooled, thereby preventing the thermal runaway phenomenon from spreading throughout the battery rack 100.

[0037] The coolant tube 150 connects the water tank 130 and the battery pack 120 to each other, and functions as a passage for carrying the coolant supplied from the water tank 130 to the battery pack 120. To perform this function, one end of the coolant tube 150 is connected to the water tank 130, and the other end of the coolant tube 150 is branched by the number of the battery packs 120 and connected to the plurality of battery packs 120, respectively.

[0038] If the thermal runaway phenomenon occurs in at least a part of the plurality of battery packs 120 as described above, the sensor 160 detects a temperature rise and/or a gas ejection and transmits a detection signal to the controller 140. To perform this function, the sensor 160 may be a temperature sensor or a gas detection sensor, or a combination of the temperature sensor and the gas detection sensor.

[0039] The sensor 160 is installed inside the rack housing 110 to detect temperature rise or gas generation inside the battery rack 100. The sensor 160 may be attached to an inner side or outer side of each of the plurality of battery packs 120 to quickly sense the temperature of the battery pack 120 and/or gas generated from the battery pack 120.
[0040] Next, the battery pack 120 applied to the battery rack 100 according to an embodiment of the present disclosure will be described in more detail with reference to FIGS. 4 to 10 .

[0041] Referring to FIGS. 4 to 10 , the battery pack 120 may be implemented to include a plurality of battery cells 121, a bus bar frame 122, a pack housing 123, an air inlet 124, an air outlet 125 and an expansion pad 127. In addition, the battery pack 120 may further include a swelling absorption pad 126 in addition to the above components.

[0042] The battery cell 121 is provided in plural, and the plurality of battery cells 121 are stacked to form one unit module 121A. Also, a plurality of unit modules 121A are stacked to form a single unit module stack. As the battery cell 121, for example, a pouch-type battery cell may be applied. The battery cell 121 includes a pair of electrode leads 121a respectively drawn out at both sides thereof in a longitudinal direction.

[0043] The bus bar frame 122 is provided in a pair, and the pair of bus bar frames 122 cover one side and the other side of the unit module stack in a width direction. The electrode lead of the battery cell 121 is drawn through a slit formed at the bus bar frame 122, and is bent and fixed by welding or the like onto the bus bar frame 122. That is, the plurality of battery cells 121 may be electrically connected by the bus bar frame 122.

[0044] The pack housing 123 has a substantially rectangular parallelepiped shape, and accommodates the unit module stacks therein. The air inlet 124 and the air outlet 125 are formed at one side and the other side of the pack housing 123 in the longitudinal direction.

[0045] The air inlet 124 is formed at one side of the module stack in the stacking direction, namely at one side of the battery pack 120 in the longitudinal direction and has a hole shape formed through the pack housing 123. The air outlet 125 is formed at the other side of the module stack in the stacking direction, namely at the other side of the battery pack 120 in the longitudinal direction and is has a hole shape formed through the pack housing 123.
[0046] The air inlet 124 and the air outlet 125 are located at diagonally opposite sides along the longitudinal direction of the battery pack 120.

[0047] Meanwhile, an empty space is formed between the bus bar frame 122 and the pack housing 123. That is, the empty space in which air for cooling the battery cell 121 flows is formed between one of six surfaces of the pack housing 123 facing one side and the other side of the battery cell 121 in the longitudinal direction and the bus bar frame 122. The empty space is formed at each of both sides of the battery pack 120 in the width direction.

[0048] The air inlet 124 is formed at a location corresponding to the empty space formed at one side of the battery pack 120 in the width direction, and the air outlet 125 is formed at a location corresponding to the empty space formed at the other side of the battery pack 120 in the width direction.

[0049] In the battery pack 120, the air introduced therein through the air inlet 124 cools the battery cell 121 while moving from the empty space formed at one side of the battery pack 120 in the width direction to the empty space formed at the other side of the battery pack 120 in the width direction, and then goes out of the battery pack 120 through the air outlet 125. That is, the battery pack 120 corresponds to an air-cooled battery pack.

[0050] The coolant tube 150 passes through the pack housing 123 from one side or the other side of the module stack in the stacking direction and communicates with the empty space formed between the bus bar frame 122 and the pack housing 123. A coolant tube insert hole 123a into which the coolant tube 150 may be inserted is formed at a surface among six surfaces of the pack housing 123, where the air inlet 124 or the air outlet 125 is formed. The coolant tube insert hole 123a communicates with the empty space, and the coolant tube 150 is inserted into the battery pack 120 through the coolant tube insert hole 123a. The coolant tube insert hole 123a may be formed at a side opposite to the air inlet 124 or the air outlet 125 along the width direction of the battery pack 120.

[0051] The coolant introduced into the battery pack 120 through the coolant tube 150 flows from the empty space formed at one side of the battery pack 120 in the width direction to the empty space formed at the other side of the battery pack 120 in the width direction to fill the inside of the battery pack 120, as is shown in FIGS. 4 and 5 .

[0052] Referring to FIGS. 7 to 9 , the battery pack 120 may include a swelling absorption pad 126 interposed between unit modules 121A of the module stack. The swelling absorption pad 126 may include, for example, materials such as silicon, graphite, expanded polypropylene (EPP), expanded polystylene (EPS), and the like, and has elasticity to absorb volume expansion of the battery cell 121 caused by swelling.

[0053] Referring to FIGS. 7 and 8 , the swelling absorption pad 126 includes a coolant channel P that provides a path through which the coolants may flow, so that the coolant may cool the battery cell 121 while passing between unit modules 121A adjacent to each other.

[0054] The coolant channel P includes an input port 126a formed at one side of the swelling absorption pad 126 in the longitudinal direction, an output port 126b formed at the other side of the swelling absorption pad 126 in the longitudinal direction, and a cooling portion 126c connecting the input port 126a and the output port 126b to each other.
[0055] The coolant channel P is open so that the coolant flowing through the coolant channel P directly contacts the pair of battery cells 121 in contact with the swelling absorption pad 126.

[0056] The coolant flowing into the empty space formed at one side of the battery pack 120 in the width direction sequentially passes through the input port 126a, the cooling portion 126c and the output port 126b, and moves to the empty space formed at the other side of the battery pack 120 in the width direction to come into contact with the battery cell 121, thereby cooling the battery cell 121.

[0057] The cooling portion 126c has a greater sectional area than the input port 126a and the output port 126b so that the coolant entering between the battery cells 121 adjacent to each other through the input port 126a may stay as long as possible.

[0058] As a result, the coolant introduced through the input port 126a has a slow flow rate in the cooling portion 126c and has sufficient time to contact the battery cell 121. After completely exchanging heat with the battery cell 121, the coolant exits through the output port 126b.

[0059] Meanwhile, referring to FIG. 9 , the input port 126a may be located higher than the output port 126b. If the input port 126a may be located higher than the output port 126b as described above, the coolant may flow more smoothly, thereby improving the cooling efficiency.

[0060] Referring to FIG. 10 , the expansion pad 127 is disposed inside the air inlet 124 and the air outlet 125, and has a size smaller than the opened area of the air inlet 124 and the air outlet 125. The expansion pad 127 preferably has a size of less than 30% compared to the opened area of the air inlet 124 and air outlet 125 so that the air may flow through the air inlet 124 and the air outlet 125 smoothly when the battery module 120 is normally used.

[0061] The expansion pad 127 is expanded by contacting the coolant introduced into the battery pack 120 to close the air inlet 124 and the air outlet 125. The expansion pad 126 contains a resin that exhibits a very large expansion rate when absorbing moisture, for example a resin that increases in volume by at least two times or more compared to the initial volume when a sufficient amount of moisture is provided thereto. As a resin used for the expansion pad 127, a polyester staple fiber is mentioned, for example.

[0062] By applying the expansion pad 127, when a thermal runaway phenomenon occurs in at least some battery packs 120 and thus a coolant is introduced into the battery packs 120, the air inlet 124 and the air outlet 125 are closed. If the air inlet 124 and the air outlet 125 are closed as above, the coolant introduced into the battery pack 120 does not escape to the outside but stays inside the battery pack 120, thereby quickly resolving the thermal runaway phenomenon occurring in the battery packs 120.
[0063] Next, a battery rack according to another embodiment of the present disclosure will be described with reference to FIG. 11 .

[0064] The battery rack according to another embodiment of the present disclosure is different from the battery rack 100 according to an embodiment of the present disclosure described above only in the point that a valve 170 is installed inside the coolant tube 150, and other components are substantially the same.

[0065] Thus, the battery rack according to another embodiment of the present disclosure will be described based on the valve 170, and the features identical to the former embodiment will not be described in detail.

[0066] The valve 170 is provided in plural as much as the number of the plurality of battery packs 120, and the valves 170 are respectively installed adjacent to the plurality of battery packs 120 to individually allow or block the flow of coolant flowing into the plurality of battery packs 120.

[0067] As described above, in order to operate the plurality of valves 170 independently, at least one sensor 160 is provided for each battery pack 120. Thus, if the sensor 160 is provided for every battery pack 120, it is possible to input the coolant only to some battery packs 120 in which a thermal runaway phenomenon occurs.

[0068] That is, if the controller 140 receives a detection signal from some sensors 160, the controller 140 determines that a thermal runaway phenomenon occurs in the battery packs 120 to which the sensors 160 sending the detection signal are attached, and opens the valves 170 installed adjacent to the battery packs 120 where the thermal runaway phenomenon occurs among the plurality of valves 170 so that the coolant may be put thereto.
